$comment: NEW 2026-08-28. Built because Alation's own `Fetch DQ Standards` cannot do
this job: its input schema is empty (properties: {}, additionalProperties
false), it reads table_metadata off the conversation payload rather than
from arguments, it returns candidate checks grouped by column_id, and it is
alation_internal — invisible in Agent Studio without an FDE flip. It is a
purpose-built helper for a DQ recommendation agent, coupled to that agent's
input contract. Do not mistake it for a standards reader.
WHAT DEPENDS ON THIS: the reconciler agent, and the lifecycle Flow. A
PUBLISHED overlay standard can be edited but NOT deleted, so before anything
creates a standard, something has to read what already exists and fuzzy-match
against it. This is that read. Getting it wrong leaves permanent objects in a
customer instance.
GET on the same base path the create tool POSTs to, with the same auth block
— which the kit has already proven answers 200 (`policy standards` reads it).
Note that success there was with bearer AND CDEToken; this tool sends bearer
only, same open question as the create tool.
The response carries each standard's integer `id` and UUID `key`. The
id-taking path is /standard/{id}/, so an agent reasoning about updates must
use the integer. Standards also carry `status` — only PUBLISHED ones are
applied by CDM, so a DRAFT standard is not yet governing anything and the
reconciler must report the status, not just existence.
THIS IS A LIST, AND A LIST IS A SUMMARY — verified 2026-09-03 by reading all
19 items on finance-industry.mtse. Each carries id, name, key, type, version,
status, derived_standards_count, owners, sources and timestamps. It gives the
COUNT of derived requirements and NOT their content, so an agent cannot learn
what a standard obliges from this call. Use `Fetch CDE Overlay Standard
Detail` for that. Three cde_creator runs tried to read requirements here,
failed, and silently fell back to the source policy's prose.
IT RETURNS EVERY VERSION, AND VERSIONS CAN HAVE DIFFERENT NAMES. `key` is the
standard's stable identity; `id` + `version` identify one version. On this
instance six BCBS239 standards each have a version 2 named `Test 1`..`Test 6`
— the SAME key as the BCBS239-named version 1, not separate objects. So a
caller that matches on name alone will pick a superseded version, and a caller
that takes the first row for a key may pick either. Group by `key` and take
the highest `version` with status PUBLISHED.
name: Fetch CDE Overlay Standards
description: List the CDE overlay standards that exist in this Alation instance, with their integer id, name, purpose, scope, status, source policy and full derived_requirements. Use this before creating any standard, to check whether an equivalent one already exists — a published standard can be edited but never deleted, so creating a duplicate is permanent. Also use it to compare what a regulation now requires against what the instance already governs. Status matters: only PUBLISHED standards are applied by CDM, so a DRAFT standard exists but is not yet governing anything.
